# Appeal of Denial — Total Ankle Replacement (CPT 27702)

**RE: Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-01**
**Member:** Sawyer Foster
**Member ID:** W558551284
**Reference Number:** POC-64107D6EF7-65599
**Governing Policy:** Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines: Small Joint Surgery (Carelon), effective 11/05/2023 — https://files.providernews.anthem.com/2519/PDF-Small-Joint-Surgery-2023-11-05.pdf

Dear Anthem Blue Cross Blue Shield Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my request for a total ankle replacement (CPT 27702). My surgeon, Dr. Okafor, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I am asking that this decision be reconsidered.

## Why I am appealing

The denial notice states that "the documentation submitted was incomplete and does not allow a determination of medical necessity." I understand this to mean the plan could not confirm that my records meet its own criteria for ankle arthroplasty. I believe the records already submitted meet most of those criteria, and I am identifying below exactly where the record stands and where additional documentation may still be needed.

The governing policy states that ankle arthroplasty "is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met":

> "• Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint • Significant pain and functional impairment due to arthritis of the ankle persist after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management • Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion (e.g., strong, palpable pedal pulses) • Device is FDA approved"

Here is how my records correspond to each element:

**1. Radiographic confirmation of advanced/end-stage arthritis of the tibiotalar joint.**
Weight-bearing ankle radiographs taken 2026-06-05 showed tibiotalar joint space obliteration with subchondral cysts. This is documented imaging evidence of advanced joint disease.

**2. Significant pain and functional impairment persisting after at least 3 months of supervised conservative management.**
I completed 14 weeks of supervised physical therapy (2026-03-09 through 2026-06-15, 18 visits), which is documented in the physical therapy discharge note. I also used NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief, and had a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-16 that gave only 4 weeks of partial relief. This is well beyond the 3-month conservative-management period referenced in the policy.

The policy also defines "significant pain and functional impairment" as:

> "pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes."

My records show I ambulate with an antalgic gait and am limited to walking two blocks, and that I have positive provocative testing and pain-limited range of motion on exam. [Placeholder: documented VAS pain score, if not already in the chart, and a second impacted daily activity beyond walking, such as difficulty with footwear, to fully match this definition]

**3. Documentation of adequate lower extremity vascular perfusion.**
[Placeholder: documentation of pedal pulse examination or other vascular perfusion assessment, if not already included in the surgical workup]

**4. Device is FDA approved.**
[Placeholder: manufacturer/device documentation confirming FDA approval of the specific implant proposed by Dr. Okafor, if not already submitted with the prior authorization request]

I have not had a prior ankle reconstruction, so the revision criteria in the policy do not apply to my case.

## What I am asking

I am asking Anthem to reconsider this denial in light of the conservative-management, imaging, and functional documentation already in my file, and to identify specifically what additional information — such as vascular exam findings or device FDA status — is needed to complete the medical necessity review. I understand the plan's policy states that Carelon "applies objective and evidence-based criteria" and takes "individual circumstances" into account, and I am asking that my full clinical picture be considered under that standard.

Please treat this letter as my formal request for internal appeal. I understand this appeal must be received by 2027-01-28, and I am submitting it to the appeal address printed on my denial letter, as instructed. I can also be reached to provide any additional records needed to complete this review.

Thank you for reconsidering my case.

Sincerely,

_________________________
Sawyer Foster
Member ID: W558551284
Date: [insert date of mailing]
Contact phone/email: [insert contact information]

---

*This letter is not medical or legal advice and does not guarantee that coverage will be approved.*

21 Revision Total Ankle Arthroplasty Revision total ankle arthroplasty is considered medically necessary in skeletally mature patients when ALL of the following criteria are met:
If conservative management is not appropriate, the reason must be clearly documented.

Conservative management offered by the provider or other health professionals for this condition(s) should include footwear modification and/or padding/accommodative devices (e.g., foot orthosis) AND at least one of the following complementary strategies to reduce inflammation, alleviate pain, and improve function:

• Activity modification • Anti-inflammatory medications and analgesics • Corticosteroid injection(s) • Debridement of associated hyperkeratotic lesions, such as corns or calluses Documentation of compliance with a plan of therapy that includes elements from these areas is required where conservative management is appropriate.
If conservative management is not appropriate, the medical record must clearly document why such an approa ch is not reasonable.

For the purposes of this guideline, significant pain and functional impairment refer to pain rated ≥ 4 on the VAS scale and associated with difficulty performing at least 2 impacted daily activities, such as walking and wearing reasonable shoes.
Adherence to a tobacco cessation program resulting in abstinence from tobacco for at least 6 weeks prior to surgery is strongly recommended.

Where there are patient-specific modifiable comorbidities that may adversely impact patient reported outcomes or the health status of the patient a shared decision-making process with the patient to discuss these modifiable comorbidities is strongly recommended and should be documented.
